name: idpf_vc_core_init
prose: Initialises virtchnl communication with the device and the per-adapter software state (idpf_virtchnl.c:3422-3591; slice cut the head). It allocates adapter->vcxn_mngr if needed (-ENOMEM goes to init_failed) and initialises its transactions. A state loop then runs the version check (idpf_send_ver_msg: 0 advances to __IDPF_GET_CAPS and sleeps 30 ms, -EAGAIN retries after the sleep, any other error goes to init_failed) and the get-capabilities message (an error goes to init_failed; success sets __IDPF_INIT_SW and leaves the loop); any other adapter state logs 'Device is in bad state' and goes to init_failed with -EINVAL. It then obtains the LAN memory regions (idpf_send_get_lan_memory_regions, failure returns -EINVAL) or calculates the remaining BAR regions (failure returns -ENOMEM), maps them (failure returns -ENOMEM), sets the SR-IOV VF count and allocates the vports array (-ENOMEM, returned directly without unwinding the earlier steps), the netdevs array and the vport params buffer (failures go to err_netdev_alloc which frees the vports array and returns err), sets max_vports, starts the mailbox and service delayed work, requests interrupt vectors (failure cancels both works, releases the params buffer and frees the vports array via err_intr_req/err_netdev_alloc), initialises PTP (failure only logged), initialises the available queues, queues the init task, sets IDPF_VC_CORE_INIT and returns 0. The return paths that do not go through those labels (memory region/BAR errors and the vports allocation) do not undo earlier allocations such as vcxn_mngr or the mapped regions. init_failed returns err if the driver is being removed (IDPF_REMOVE_IN_PROG); after more than IDPF_MB_MAX_ERR failures (mb_wait_count) it returns -EFAULT; otherwise it resets the state to __IDPF_VER_CHECK, shuts down the transaction manager, sets IDPF_HR_DRV_LOAD, queues the vc_event_task (not the init_task) and returns -EAGAIN.
note: Reviewers: original (failure paths such as vports kcalloc do not unwind all earlier allocations) right: 3500-3503, 3474-3496; round-2 (vcxn_mngr kzalloc failure goes through init_failed, which may reset state) right: 3428-3433, 3569-3590; round-15 (init_failed queues vc_event_task, not init_task) right: 3587. 3/3 right. Whole function read; slice cut the head.

name: idpf_set_promiscuous
prose: Sends the virtchnl2 promiscuous-mode configuration for a vport (idpf_virtchnl.c:4340-4373; the packet name idpf_send_config_promiscuous_mode is not the real name and the slice cut the head). It builds a VIRTCHNL2_OP_CONFIG_PROMISCUOUS_MODE message whose flags field has VIRTCHNL2_UNICAST_PROMISC if __IDPF_PROMISC_UC is set in config_data->user_flags and VIRTCHNL2_MULTICAST_PROMISC if __IDPF_PROMISC_MC is set (flags 0 if neither), with vport_id as given; only those two fields of the message are filled. It issues the transaction with idpf_vc_xn_exec in asynchronous mode (it does not wait for a reply) and returns the negative error of idpf_vc_xn_exec if that is negative, else 0.
note: Packet name wrong; real function idpf_set_promiscuous (idpf_virtchnl.c:4340). Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: igb_read_part_string
prose: Reads the board assembly (PBA) number from the NVM into a caller buffer (e1000_nvm.c, 'igb_read_part_string' at about line 480-575; the packet name igb_read_pba_number is not the real name and the slice cut the head). Returns E1000_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT if part_num is NULL. It reads NVM words at NVM_PBA_OFFSET_0 and NVM_PBA_OFFSET_1 (a failed read returns that error). If the first word is not the NVM_PBA_PTR_GUARD value the number is in legacy format: it needs part_num_size >= 11, otherwise returns E1000_ERR_NO_SPACE; it then builds an 10-character string 'XXXXXX-XXX' with a '-' at index 6 and NUL at index 10 by converting nibbles of the two words to hex characters, and returns 0. Otherwise the second word is a pointer to a length-prefixed string: it reads the length (read error returned), returns E1000_ERR_NVM_PBA_SECTION if the length is 0 or 0xFFFF, returns E1000_ERR_NO_SPACE if part_num_size < length*2 - 1, then reads length-1 words after the length word, storing two bytes per word (high byte first) and NUL-terminates; a read error returns that error with the buffer partly written. Returns 0 on success.
note: Packet name wrong; slice cut the head. Real function igb_read_part_string (e1000_nvm.c:478-576). Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: igb_tsync_interrupt
prose: Handles the TimeSync interrupt of an igb adapter (igb_main.c:7056-7094; slice cut the head). It reads E1000_TSICR; on an 82580 it also writes back tsicr & mask to clear the cause (a hardware workaround). If the SYS_WRAP bit is set it prepares a PTP_CLOCK_PPS event and reports it with ptp_clock_event only when adapter->ptp_caps.pps is non-zero. If the TXTS bit is set it schedules ptp_tx_work. For TT0/TT1 it calls igb_perout for pin 0/1 and for AUTT0/AUTT1 igb_extts for pin 0/1. Those two helpers return without effect if no valid pin is assigned (ptp_find_pin result out of range). igb_perout always takes adapter->tmreg_lock while it works, but igb_extts takes tmreg_lock only on 82580, i354 and i350 (around the timecounter conversion); on other MACs it reads the AUX stamp registers without that lock and posts a PTP_CLOCK_EXTTS event. The function returns nothing.
note: Reviewers: original (SYS_WRAP PPS event is conditional on ptp_caps.pps) right: 7074-7075; round-15 (igb_extts does not always take tmreg_lock; only on 82580/i354/i350) right: igb_main.c 7035-7048. 2/2 right. Slice cut the head.

name: igb_rcv_msg_from_vf
prose: Reads one mailbox message from a VF and answers it (igb_main.c:8040-8121; slice cut the head). The VF's mailbox is released by whichever path the function takes, per the comments at 8067 and 8115: igb_unlock_mbx at the unlock label, igb_write_mbx for replies, or inside igb_vf_reset_msg. It reads up to E1000_VFMAILBOX_SIZE words with igb_read_mbx. If the read fails it logs, clears IGB_VF_FLAG_CTS and then either unlocks silently (if less than 2 s have passed since last_nack) or goes to the reply with a NACK and no CTS bit. A message that already has ACK or NACK set is ignored (unlock, no reply). E1000_VF_RESET calls igb_vf_reset_msg and returns (no CTS/ACK/NACK reply from this function). If the VF has not got IGB_VF_FLAG_CTS set it unlocks silently within 2 s of last_nack, else replies NACK without setting CTS. Otherwise it dispatches on the low 16 bits: set MAC address, promiscuous, multicast, LPE, VLAN (refused with a warning when an administrative pf_vlan is set), anything else logs 'Unhandled Msg' and counts as failure; it then ORs E1000_VT_MSGTYPE_CTS into the reply and sets ACK if the handler returned 0, otherwise NACK, and writes the one-word reply with igb_write_mbx. So only replies to commands that reached the dispatch carry CTS; the read-failure and not-CTS replies carry NACK only.
note: Reviewers: original (reset and already-ACKed messages return without CTS/ACK/NACK reply; read-failure path may write instead of unlock) right: 8060-8070, 8050-8056; round-2 (non-CTS reply sets NACK but not CTS) right: 8072-8077 jumps to out past 8107; round-15 (early read-failure / CTS-clear NACK replies skip setting CTS) right. 3/3 right. I did not read igb_vf_reset_msg, igb_unlock_mbx or igb_write_mbx; the unlock behaviour is taken from the comments at 8067 and 8115.

name: igb_ptp_set_timestamp_mode
prose: Programs the hardware timestamping mode from a hwtstamp request (igb_ptp.c:1132-1276; slice cut the head). It may rewrite config->rx_filter to what the hardware actually does. tx_type HWTSTAMP_TX_OFF disables TX stamping, HWTSTAMP_TX_ON enables it, any other value returns -ERANGE. Rx filters: NONE disables RX stamping; V1 L4 sync/delay-request select the V1 L4 mode; the V2 filters are all mapped to PTP_V2_EVENT (L2 and L4 matching, config->rx_filter rewritten); V1 L4 event, NTP_ALL and ALL select timestamp-all and rewrite the filter to ALL, except on the 82576 which cannot do that and, like any unsupported value, sets config->rx_filter to NONE and returns -ERANGE. On an 82575 it returns -EINVAL if either TX or RX stamping would be enabled, else 0, without touching registers. On 82580 and newer, if any RX filter is requested it forces timestamp-all (config->rx_filter becomes ALL, L2 and L4 matching) and on i210/i211 sets RXPBS_CFG_TS_EN. It then writes TSYNCTXCTL, TSYNCRXCTL, TSYNCRXCFG, the 1588 ethertype filter (enabled only when L2 is selected, else zeroed) and, when L4 is selected, IMIR(3), IMIREXT(3), FTQF(3) (and SPQF(3) on 82576); when L4 is not selected it writes only FTQF(3) with the mask value. After flushing, it reads TXSTMPL/H and RXSTMPL/H to clear stale timestamps and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original (82580+ forces rx_filter to ALL) right: 1208-1212; round-2 (IMIR(3)/IMIREXT(3) only when is_l4) right: 1248-1266; round-15 (code only reads TSYNCTXCTL/TSYNCRXCTL control registers, not the timestamp registers) WRONG: 1270-1273 read TXSTMPL/H and RXSTMPL/H. 2 right, 1 wrong. Slice cut the head.

name: e1000_poll_for_msg
prose: Polls the igbvf mailbox until a message from the PF is seen (mbx.c:13-31). countdown starts at hw->mbx.timeout. If mbx.ops.check_for_msg is NULL it skips polling and returns E1000_SUCCESS only if countdown (that is, mbx.timeout) is non-zero, otherwise -E1000_ERR_MBX; in that case mbx.timeout is not modified. Otherwise it loops while countdown is non-zero and check_for_msg(hw) returns non-zero (no message yet), decrementing countdown and waiting mbx->usec_delay microseconds each time. If countdown reaches 0 (timeout, or the initial timeout was already 0) it sets mbx->timeout = 0 so later posts fail until reset and returns -E1000_ERR_MBX; otherwise it returns E1000_SUCCESS.
note: Reviewers: original (SUCCESS when check_for_msg is NULL, not only when a message was seen) right for the timeout != 0 case; round-2 (returns -ERR if timeout is 0 even with NULL op) right: 30; round-15 (timeout not zeroed when check_for_msg is NULL) right: 18-19 skip 27-28. 3/3 right.

name: e1000_poll_for_ack
prose: Polls the igbvf mailbox until the PF acknowledges a message (mbx.c:39-57). countdown starts at hw->mbx.timeout. If mbx.ops.check_for_ack is NULL it skips polling and returns E1000_SUCCESS only if mbx.timeout is non-zero, otherwise -E1000_ERR_MBX; mbx.timeout is not modified in that case. Otherwise it loops while countdown is non-zero and check_for_ack(hw) returns non-zero, decrementing countdown and waiting mbx->usec_delay microseconds each time. If countdown reaches 0 it sets mbx->timeout = 0 (later posts fail until reset) and returns -E1000_ERR_MBX; otherwise it returns E1000_SUCCESS.
note: Reviewers: same three claims as for e1000_poll_for_msg, all right: 44-45, 53-56. 3/3 right.

name: igc_probe
prose: PCI probe for the Intel igc driver (igc_main.c:7108-7371; slice cut the head). If pci_enable_device_mem fails it returns that error directly (no pci_disable_device). Every later failure sets err and goes to one of the labels, all of which end at pci_disable_device and return err: no usable 64-bit DMA mask (err_dma), pci_request_mem_regions failing (err_pci_reg), alloc_etherdev_mq failing (-ENOMEM, err_alloc_etherdev), pci_save_state failing or ioremap of BAR 0 failing (-EIO) (err_ioremap, which frees the netdev), ei->get_invariants or igc_sw_init failing (err_sw_init), an NVM checksum that does not validate (when a flash is present) or an invalid MAC address (-EIO to err_eeprom), and register_netdev failing (err_register, which also releases hardware control and stops PTP). Unwind order: err_register, err_eeprom (reset the PHY if resets are not blocked), err_sw_init (clear the interrupt scheme and iounmap), err_ioremap (free_netdev), err_alloc_etherdev (release memory regions), err_pci_reg/err_dma (pci_disable_device). A PTM-enable failure is only logged. On success it sets up features, MTU range, MAC address, timers and work items, WoL, PTP, TSN and FPE state, resets the hardware, takes hardware control, registers the netdev, turns the carrier off, disables EEE, drops the runtime-PM reference with pm_runtime_put_noidle and (with CONFIG_IGC_LEDS) sets up the LEDs (a failure is only warned about), and returns 0.
note: Reviewer (not every failure path calls pci_disable_device: pci_enable_device_mem failure returns directly) is right: 7116-7119. Slice cut the head; real function 7108-7371. I skimmed the feature-setup block 7222-7280 rather than reading every line.

name: ixgbe_set_copper_phy_power
prose: Powers a copper PHY up or down through its MDIO vendor control register (ixgbe_phy.c, 'int ixgbe_set_copper_phy_power(struct ixgbe_hw *hw, bool on)', about lines 2794-2823; the packet name ixgbe_set_phy_power is not the real name and the slice cut the head). It returns 0 without any MDIO access if the MAC's media type is not copper, or if on is false and manageability firmware is present (ixgbe_mng_present). Otherwise it reads MDIO_CTRL1 in MDIO_MMD_VEND1 through phy.ops.read_reg and returns that status if non-zero. If on is true it clears the low-power bit; if on is false and ixgbe_check_reset_blocked reports the reset is blocked it returns 0 without writing; otherwise it sets the low-power bit. It then writes the register back with phy.ops.write_reg and returns that write's status.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name is wrong; real function ixgbe_set_copper_phy_power. Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: ixgbe_check_cs4227
prose: Ensures the CS4227 retimer of an ixgbe X550EM port has been reset, coordinating with other driver instances through its scratch register (ixgbe_x550.c:227-290; slice cut the head; returns nothing). Up to IXGBE_CS4227_RETRIES times it acquires the PHY software/firmware semaphore (hw->phy.phy_semaphore_mask; on failure it logs, sleeps IXGBE_CS4227_CHECK_DELAY and retries) and reads the CS4227 scratch register: if it reads RESET_COMPLETE it goes to out; if the read failed or the value is not RESET_PENDING it breaks out of the loop; if a reset is pending it releases the semaphore, sleeps IXGBE_CS4227_CHECK_DELAY and retries. If all retries were used it tries to acquire the semaphore once more, and if that fails it logs and returns without resetting anything and without holding the semaphore. Otherwise it resets the CS4227 (ixgbe_reset_cs4227); a failure logs and goes to out (releasing the semaphore). On success it writes RESET_PENDING to the scratch register (the write status is ignored), releases the semaphore, sleeps 10-12 ms, re-acquires it (failure logs and returns without recording completion) and writes RESET_COMPLETE to the scratch register (its status is not checked). At out it releases the semaphore and sleeps hw->eeprom.semaphore_delay milliseconds. Paths that reach out hold the semaphore at that point; the two early returns do not.
note: Reviewers: original (early return when the final acquire fails leaves no RESET_COMPLETE and no reset attempted) right: 256-260, 277-281; round-2 (on reset failure code goes to out and releases the semaphore, not returns holding it) right: 265-268, 287-289; round-15 (out path sleeps IXGBE_CS4227_CHECK_DELAY, not eeprom.semaphore_delay; RESET_PENDING write status is checked) WRONG on both: 289 sleeps hw->eeprom.semaphore_delay, and the write at 273 is not checked. 2 right, 1 wrong. Slice cut the head.

name: ixgbevf_set_ringparam
prose: ethtool set-ring-parameters handler of ixgbevf (ethtool.c:236-403; slice cut the head). Returns -EINVAL if rx_mini_pending or rx_jumbo_pending is non-zero. It clamps tx_pending and rx_pending to the driver min/max and aligns them to the required descriptor multiples; if both equal the current ring counts it returns 0 immediately. These two early returns happen before __IXGBEVF_RESETTING is set, so they do not touch that bit. Otherwise it spins (usleep_range) until it can set __IXGBEVF_RESETTING. If the interface is not running it only stores the new counts in the existing rings and counters and goes to clear_reset. If it is running it allocates and sets up clone TX rings (regular and XDP) with the new count if the TX count changed, and clone RX rings if the RX count changed (an allocation failure frees what was set up and goes to clear_reset with -ENOMEM or the setup error), then brings the interface down, frees the old ring resources, copies the new rings in, updates the ring counts and brings it back up. clear_reset frees any leftover temporary TX ring array (the path taken when an RX setup fails after TX rings were allocated) and clears __IXGBEVF_RESETTING, then returns err (0 on success).
note: Reviewer (early-return path does not clear __IXGBEVF_RESETTING) is right as a statement about the code: the bit is set only at 262, after the two early returns at 247 and 260, and is cleared only at 401. Slice cut the head; real function 236-403.

name: ixgbevf_probe
prose: PCI probe for an Intel ixgbevf virtual function (ixgbevf_main.c:4557-4758; slice cut the head). If pci_enable_device fails it returns that error directly. Later failures set err and go to labels that end at pci_disable_device (done only when no adapter exists or the adapter was just marked disabled) and return err: no usable 64-bit DMA mask (err_dma), pci_request_regions failing (err_pci_reg), alloc_etherdev_mq failing (-ENOMEM, err_alloc_etherdev), BAR 0 ioremap failing (-EIO, err_ioremap, frees the netdev), four failures that go to err_sw_init: ixgbevf_sw_init failing, an invalid MAC address (-EIO), IXGBE_REMOVED(hw_addr) (-EIO) and ixgbevf_init_interrupt_scheme failing; and register_netdev failing (err_register, which clears the interrupt scheme first). err_sw_init resets interrupt capability, unmaps BAR 0 and frees the RSS key, then falls into err_ioremap. It sets up netdev ops, feature flags and the MTU range by mailbox API version, the service timer and work, registers the netdev, only then calls pci_set_drvdata, turns the carrier off, initialises IPsec offload and statistics, prints the VF type and returns 0.
note: Reviewer (says three paths but there are four goto err_sw_init paths: sw_init, invalid MAC, IXGBE_REMOVED, init_interrupt_scheme) is right: 4626, 4632, 4695, 4706. Slice cut the head; real function 4557-4758.

name: IQ_INSTR_PENDING
note: Statement-expression macro in octep_vf_main.h:35-37 ((write_index - flush_index) & ring_size_mask on the queue pointer); not a function. Dropped.

name: cpt_inline_ipsec_cfg_inbound
prose: Enables or disables inline IPsec inbound processing on one CPT LF (rvu_cpt.c:560-612; slice cut the head). It first reads CPT_AF_LFX_CTL for the LF (so the error paths below read one register). If req->enable is set and bit 16 (outbound path) is already set it returns CPT_AF_ERR_INLINE_IPSEC_INB_ENA; if req->sso_pf_func is non-zero and the pf_func is not a valid SSO mapping it returns CPT_AF_ERR_SSO_PF_FUNC_INVALID; neither of these writes anything. Otherwise it sets bit 9 of the LF control value when enabling (clears it when disabling), ORs the NIX select (1 for BLKADDR_CPT1 else 0) into bit 8 (bit 8 is never cleared here) and writes CPT_AF_LFX_CTL. If sso_pf_func is non-zero it also writes the SSO and NIX pf_func fields into CPT_AF_LFX_CTL2; if sso_pf_func_ovrd is set it writes 1 to CPT_AF_ECO; and on non-OTX2 silicon it writes the X2P link config for links 0 and 1. It returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original (omits CPT_AF_ERR_SSO_PF_FUNC_INVALID; SSO/NIX pf_funcs written only when sso_pf_func non-zero) right: 576-577, 589-595; round-2 (bit 8 is ORed, not cleared, when nix_sel is 0) right: 586; round-15 (error paths read CPT_AF_LFX_CTL before returning, so they do touch a register) right: 567. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head.

name: cpt_inline_ipsec_cfg_outbound
prose: Enables or disables inline IPsec outbound processing on one CPT LF (rvu_cpt.c:614-657; slice cut the head). It first reads CPT_AF_LFX_CTL. If req->enable is set and bit 9 (inbound path) is already set it returns CPT_AF_ERR_INLINE_IPSEC_OUT_ENA; if req->nix_pf_func is non-zero and is not a valid NIX mapping it returns CPT_AF_ERR_NIX_PF_FUNC_INVALID; neither writes anything. Otherwise it sets bit 16 when enabling (clears it when disabling) and writes CPT_AF_LFX_CTL. Only if nix_pf_func is non-zero does it also write the NIX pf_func field in CPT_AF_LFX_CTL2 and then read CPT_AF_LFX_CTL again, OR the NIX select (0 for NIX0, otherwise 1) into bit 8 (never cleared) and write it back. It returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original (omits CPT_AF_ERR_NIX_PF_FUNC_INVALID; nix_sel configured only when nix_pf_func is non-zero) right: 632-633, 642-654; round-2 (bit 8 is ORed, not cleared) right: 652; round-15 (error paths read CPT_AF_LFX_CTL first, so they touch a register) right: 622. 3/3 right.

name: rvu_npa_register_interrupts
prose: Registers and enables the four NPA admin-function interrupts of an RVU device (rvu_devlink.c:765-818; slice cut the head). It returns the negative error from rvu_get_blkaddr(rvu, BLKTYPE_NPA, 0) if the NPA block cannot be found, registering nothing. It reads the NPA_AF_INT vector offset from NPA_PRIV_AF_INT_CFG (low 10 bits); if it is 0 it logs a warning and returns 0 without registering anything. Otherwise for each of the RVU, GEN, AF_ERR and POISON (RAS) vectors it calls rvu_common_request_irq (which returns true when the IRQ was allocated and false when request_irq failed) and, only on success, writes all ones to that interrupt's enable-W1S register. If any registration fails it calls rvu_npa_unregister_interrupts and returns rc, which is false, i.e. 0, so a failed registration is reported to the caller as 0 after cleanup. If all four succeed it returns 0.
note: Round-15 reviewer (code sends rc==0 (success) to the error path) is mixed: rc here is a bool that is true on success (rvu_devlink.c:29-43 returns rvu->irq_allocated[offset]), so '!rc' correctly means failure; but the function then returns that false/0, so failures look like success to the caller. Slice cut the head; real function 765-818.

name: rvu_mbox_handler_nix_lf_alloc
prose: Mailbox handler that allocates and configures a NIX LF for a PF/VF (rvu_nix.c:1497-1745; slice cut the head). It returns, before touching hardware, NIX_AF_ERR_PARAM if any of rq_cnt, sq_cnt or cq_cnt is 0; NIX_AF_ERR_AF_LF_INVALID if the PF/VF has no NIX LF; NIX_AF_INVAL_NPA_PF_FUNC / NIX_AF_INVAL_SSO_PF_FUNC if a non-zero npa_func or sso_func (RVU_DEFAULT_PF_FUNC is replaced by the caller's own pcifunc) is not a valid mapping; NIX_AF_ERR_RSS_SIZE_INVALID if rss_sz is above the maximum or not a power of two; and NIX_AF_ERR_RSS_GRPS_INVALID if rss_sz is set and rss_grps is 0 or too large. It then resets the LF (failure returns NIX_AF_ERR_LF_RESET), allocates and programs the RQ, SQ and CQ context memory and bitmaps, the RSS contexts, the CQ interrupt and QINT contexts, sets the VLAN TPIDs, LMTST, the NPA/SSO function and queue-size fields (note cfg is not cleared first, so with npa_func == 0 it still holds the TPID value written just before), the Rx config and the Tx parse kind (for a CGX-mapped PF's VF under the CGX lock only if the pkind change is permitted). A memory allocation or RSS-init failure goes to free_mem, which frees the contexts and sets rc = -ENOMEM. For a representor device it sets the Tx channel base/count and jumps to exit, skipping nix_interface_init, the NPC default-entry disable and the Rx VTAG type-7 setup. Otherwise it initialises the interface (a failure goes to free_mem), disables the NPC default entries for this LF and sets the Rx VTAG type 7. At exit (reached on success, on the representor path and after free_mem) it fills rsp (MAC address, SQB size, channels, LSO indices, stat counts, qints/cints, link counts) and returns rc: 0 or -ENOMEM.
note: Round-15 reviewer (representor success path skips NPC default entry disable) is right: 1690-1694 jumps to exit before 1706. Slice cut the head; real function 1497-1745, read in full.

name: set_flowkey_fields
prose: Builds the NIX RX flow-key algorithm entries for a flow-key bitmask (rvu_nix.c:3991-4316, 'static int set_flowkey_fields(struct nix_rx_flowkey_alg *alg, u32 flow_cfg)'; the packet item is only the middle of this function and its name was elided). It returns -EINVAL if alg is NULL. Otherwise it clears FIELDS_PER_ALG (5) 64-bit entries of alg, saves the top four bits of flow_cfg (L3/L4 source/destination selectors, bits 31:28) and masks them out, and loops over the key-type bits (idx from 0 to the highest set bit) while fewer than 5 fields are filled and the running key offset is below MAX_KEY_OFF (40). For each bit it fills a temporary field for that key type (port channel, IPv4/IPv6 protocol, outer or inner IPv4/IPv6 address with the SIP-only/DIP-only selectors narrowing the byte count, TCP/UDP/SCTP ports, ESP/AH and the other types handled in the switch), sets field->ena, and, only if the bit is actually set in flow_cfg, copies the field into alg[nr_field] with the current key offset (ESP/AH use the L4 key offset), tracks the largest field size and advances nr_field when the field is complete; when a key-offset marker is set it advances key_off by the largest size seen and resets it. It returns 0 if all bits were processed with key_off <= MAX_KEY_OFF and otherwise NIX_AF_ERR_RSS_NOSPC_FIELD.
note: The slice was a fragment from the middle of set_flowkey_fields; fixed under the real name (rule 6). I read the head (3991-4075) and tail (4276-4316) and only the first part of the large middle switch (4076-4275), so the per-protocol cases are summarised, not enumerated.

name: rvu_mbox_handler_nix_mcast_grp_update
prose: Adds or removes multicast replication entries of a NIX multicast group (rvu_nix.c:6507-6642; slice cut the head). It returns 0 immediately, without effect, if req->num_mce_entry is 0, or the error of nix_get_struct_ptrs. It takes the group-list mutex unless req->is_af is set (the AF caller already holds it) and returns NIX_AF_ERR_INVALID_MCAST_GRP (after unlocking) if the group index is unknown. For NIX_MCAST_OP_DEL_ENTRY, if any requested pcifunc equals the group's own pcifunc it destroys the whole group through rvu_mbox_handler_nix_mcast_grp_destroy (no mce_lock taken here, no list resizing, rsp not filled) and returns 0. Otherwise it takes mce_lock and disables the group's MCAM entry if it has one. For ADD it frees the existing mce list (when non-empty), allocates a new list of prev_count + num entries, and if the allocation fails and the group has an MCAM entry it re-enables that entry and returns NIX_AF_ERR_NON_CONTIG_MCE_LIST with the old list already freed and not restored (if the group has no MCAM entry the check does not return and it continues to nix_add_mce_list_entry with the failed start index); a failure of nix_add_mce_list_entry frees the new list, reallocates one of the old size (when it had entries) and re-enables the MCAM entry. For DEL it returns NIX_AF_ERR_INVALID_MCAST_DEL_REQ if the list is empty or smaller than the request, otherwise frees the list, allocates the smaller one and removes the entries (on failure it frees and reallocates the old-size list). On success without an MCAM entry it returns the start index in rsp; with one it updates the MCAM action, re-enables the entry and fills rsp->mce_start_index. It releases mce_lock and, unless is_af, the group lock, and returns ret (0 or the errors above).
note: Reviewers: original (success path may destroy the group on DEL_ENTRY match without resizing list or setting rsp; zero-entry returns 0) right: 6521-6522, 6545-6557; round-2 (NON_CONTIG path frees the previous mce list before failing; old list not left unchanged) right: 6568-6580; round-15 (destroy path with empty mce list skips mce_lock and mcam/list removal) right for this function: the destroy path at 6545-6557 returns before 6560 mce_lock. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head.

name: rvu_npc_exact_alloc_id
prose: Allocates a sequence id from the exact-match table's id bitmap (rvu_npc_hash.c:519-542; the packet name was truncated and the slice cut the head). rvu->hw->table must exist and the caller must not hold table->lock. It takes table->lock, finds the first zero bit in table->id_bmap (tot_ids bits). If none is free it unlocks, logs 'No space in id bitmap' with dev_err and returns false without writing *seq_id. Otherwise it sets that bit, unlocks, stores the index in *seq_id, logs it at debug level and returns true.
note: Name truncated in packet; real function rvu_npc_exact_alloc_id (rvu_npc_hash.c:519). Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: otx2_dma_map_skb_frag
prose: DMA-maps one segment of an skb for transmit on an otx2 NIC (otx2_common.c:2105-2131; slice cut the head) and returns the dma_addr_t from otx2_dma_map_page (which can be an error address). seg 0 is the linear part (skb->data, *len = skb_headlen) and seg n > 0 is fragment n - 1 (page, offset and *len from the fragment); seg must not exceed nr_frags. *len is always written before the mapping call. If the skb has an xfrm (IPsec) offload it uses DMA_BIDIRECTIONAL and replaces skb with the result of skb_unshare(skb, GFP_ATOMIC); that result is not checked, so if skb_unshare fails (returns NULL) the following skb->data or skb_shinfo(skb) access dereferences NULL. Otherwise the direction is DMA_TO_DEVICE. It has no other side effects.
note: Round-15 reviewer (precondition 'not shared' does not ensure skb_unshare cannot fail; code dereferences NULL unchecked) is right: 2114-2121. Slice cut the head; real function 2105-2131.

name: otx2_xdp_rcv_pkt_handler
prose: Runs the XDP program on one received otx2 packet and acts on its verdict (otx2_txrx.c:1488-1584; the packet name otx2_xdp_handle_verdict is not the real name and the slice cut the head). It returns true when the packet buffer has been consumed (transmitted, redirected successfully, or dropped) and false when the caller should continue normal processing or the buffer was not consumed. With an XSK pool it takes the buffer from pool->xdp[--xdp_top] (returning false if that is NULL), sets its data_end from the CQE segment size and runs the program; otherwise it builds an xdp_buff from the page at the segment address. For XDP_PASS it stores xdp.data - xdp.data_meta in *metasize (in the XSK case this reads the local xdp, which only the non-XSK path initialises) and returns false. XDP_TX increments cq->pool_ptrs, converts to a frame and returns the result of otx2_xdp_sq_append_pkt. XDP_REDIRECT increments pool_ptrs and calls xdp_do_redirect: on success it sets *need_xdp_flush and returns true; on failure with an XSK buffer it returns false, and on failure with a normal buffer it unmaps the page, returns the frame with xdp_return_frame and returns false. An unknown verdict logs bpf_warn_invalid_xdp_action; XDP_ABORTED also traces an exception; these and XDP_DROP increment pool_ptrs, free an XSK buffer, or recycle the page to the page pool (when it has one) or unmap and put_page it, and return true.
note: Packet name wrong; slice cut the head; real function otx2_xdp_rcv_pkt_handler (otx2_txrx.c:1488). Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: prestera_port_close
prose: ndo_stop for a Marvell Prestera port (prestera_main.c:187-220; slice cut the head). It always calls netif_stop_queue(dev). If the port has a phylink instance it stops and disconnects phylink, reads the MAC config with prestera_port_cfg_mac_read and, only if that read returned 0, clears cfg_mac.admin and writes it back (the write's return value is ignored); the return value is the MAC-read error, 0 otherwise. Without phylink and with an SFP transceiver it does the same MAC read, admin-clear and ignored write, returning the read's error. Without phylink and with another transceiver it sets port->cfg_phy.admin to false and returns the result of prestera_hw_port_phy_mode_set. So the function can return a non-zero error, and a failed MAC write is not reported.
note: Reviewers: original (ignores prestera_port_cfg_mac_write errors; can return 0 with admin not disabled) right: 201, 208; round-2 and round-15 (return value is not always 0; cfg_mac_read failure is propagated in phylink/SFP branches) right: 198-199, 205-206, 219. 3/3 right. Slice cut the head; real function 187-220.

name: prestera_util_nhc2nc_key_wrapper_unused
note: No function with this name exists in prestera_router.c (the slice lines 1-251 contain other functions such as prestera_util_nhc2nc_key); the item is not a function in the source. Dropped.

name: mtk_probe
prose: Platform-driver probe for the MediaTek frame engine (mtk_eth_soc.c:5112-5401; slice cut the head). It allocates the mtk_eth structure with devm_kzalloc and maps the register region; these and several early steps return directly without cleanup labels: -ENOMEM, the ioremap error, -EINVAL for an unsupported DMA-mask setup, missing ethsys or infra regmaps, and the error of mtk_sgmii_init. After SGMII init, failures set err and jump: err_destroy_sgmii (missing pctl regmap, missing memory resource, SRAM pool setup failures), err_wed_exit (mtk_get_irqs, clock lookup failures including -EPROBE_DEFER, and later steps up to hardware init), err_deinit_hw, err_free_dev (IRQ requests, MDIO init, clock/dummy setup), err_deinit_ppe and err_unreg_netdev (PPE init, dummy netdev allocation, register_netdev failures). The labels unwind in order: mtk_unreg_dev, cancel pending work and free the dummy netdev and its NAPI, mtk_ppe_deinit, mtk_mdio_cleanup, mtk_free_dev, mtk_hw_deinit, mtk_wed_exit, mtk_sgmii_destroy, then return err. So not every failure path runs every cleanup: a failure enters the chain at its own label and only the later steps run, and the early returns bypass the chain. On success it registers each netdev, sets drvdata, schedules the DMA monitor work and returns 0.
note: Reviewer (not every failure path runs the full cleanup; early returns bypass the labels and some go to err_destroy_sgmii) is right: 5121-5189, 5198-5221, 5376-5400. Slice cut the head; real function 5112-5401. I read the early part and the cleanup labels in full and the middle (hardware init, WED, MAC creation) via the label structure only.

name: wed_rxinfo_show
prose: debugfs show handler printing MediaTek WED receive-side registers (mtk_wed_debugfs.c:154-274; an ordinary function, not macro generated: 'static int wed_rxinfo_show(struct seq_file *s, void *data)'). data is unused; s->private is the struct mtk_wed_hw. If hw->wed_dev is non-NULL it dumps the common register table (WPDMA RX, WED RX, RRO, WDMA, RX buffer manager entries) with dump_wed_regs and then, if mtk_wed_is_v2(hw), the v2 table (route QM counters), otherwise the v3 table (RRO data, MSDU page, indirect command, address element and route QM counters). If wed_dev is NULL it prints nothing. Its only return statement returns 0 in every case.
note: The old prose called this a generated function; it is a plain function (line 154-156), unlike wed_txinfo which uses DEFINE_SHOW_ATTRIBUTE. Slice cut the head; real function 156-274.

name: mlx4_master_activate_admin_state
prose: Copies the administrative VF port settings into the operational state for a slave on the mlx4 master (cmd.c:1995-2057; slice cut the head). For each port in the slave's active-port mask it copies enable_smi to the operational smi_enabled flag and then copies vlan_proto, default_vlan and default_qos from admin to oper state only unless the admin VLAN protocol is 802.1AD and the slave does not support QinQ (vst_qinq_supported); in that case those three fields are left unchanged. It always copies link_state, mac, spoofchk, tx_rate, qos_vport and guid. If the admin default_vlan is not MLX4_VGT it registers that VLAN with __mlx4_register_vlan (the VLAN index goes into vp_oper->vlan_idx; it is the admin default_vlan that is registered, even where state.default_vlan was not updated by the check above); on failure it sets vlan_idx to NO_INDX, sets state.default_vlan to MLX4_VGT and state.vlan_proto to 802.1Q, warns and returns that error immediately, leaving later ports unprocessed. If spoofchk is set it registers the admin MAC with __mlx4_register_mac; a negative result is stored as the error (mac_idx set to NO_INDX), warned about and returned at once. It returns 0 after all ports succeed. It does not undo registrations already made on earlier ports or earlier in the same port when it returns an error.
note: Reviewers: round-1 (vlan_proto/default_vlan/default_qos not copied for 8021AD without QinQ) right: 2011-2016; round-2 and round-15 (VLAN registered while state.default_vlan was left unchanged, so deactivate may release the wrong VLAN) right about this function (2014, 2025 register vp_admin->default_vlan), but I did not read the deactivate function, so the release-side claim is unchecked. 3 right (2 only partly checked). Slice cut the head.

name: mlx4_en_filter_rfs_expire
prose: Expires old accelerated-RFS filters of an mlx4 Ethernet port (en_netdev.c:444-475; slice cut the head; returns nothing). The caller does not hold priv->filters_lock. Under filters_lock (spin_lock_bh) it scans priv->filters from the first entry for at most MLX4_EN_FILTER_EXPIRY_QUOTA + 1 entries (the check i > QUOTA stops it). A filter that is activated, has no pending work and for which rps_may_expire_flow returns true is moved to a local delete list and removed from its hash chain; any other filter is remembered as last_filter. After the scan, if last_filter is set and is not the first entry of the list, it moves the list head itself to just after last_filter (list_move(&priv->filters, &last_filter->next)), which rotates the list so the next scan starts at the entry following last_filter and the entries scanned before it go to the end. It then drops the lock and frees each filter on the delete list with mlx4_en_filter_free (outside the lock).
note: Reviewers: original (rotation moves the head after last_filter->next, so scan resumes after that node) right: 468-469; round-2 (condition tests last_filter != first, not tail; last_filter becomes last) right: 468 compares &last_filter->next with priv->filters.next; round-15 (list_move uses last_filter->next, next scan skips a node) mixed: the call is as stated, but the entries scanned before last_filter move to the end of the list rather than being skipped. 2 right, 1 mixed. Slice cut the head.

name: mlx4_en_reset_config
prose: Applies a new hardware-timestamping configuration and RX VLAN/FCS offload setting to an mlx4 port by rebuilding its resources (en_netdev.c, 'int mlx4_en_reset_config(struct net_device *dev, struct hwtstamp_config ts_config, netdev_features_t features)' at about line 3513-3604; the slice shows only the tail and its name was elided). It returns 0 at once if the TX type, RX filter and the VLAN-RX and RXFCS feature bits are all unchanged; returns -EINVAL if it is asked to turn RX VLAN offload on while an RX timestamp filter is active; returns -ENOMEM if the temporary private structure cannot be allocated. It then takes mdev->state_lock, builds a new port profile with the new timestamp config and tries to allocate the new resources (an error goes to out). If the port is up it stops it, swaps in the new resources, updates dev->features: VLAN RX and RXFCS follow the requested features, or the wanted features when RX timestamping is off; and it always clears NETIF_F_HW_VLAN_CTAG_RX (warning if it was on) when an RX timestamp filter is requested. If the port was up it restarts it (a failure is logged and kept as the error), and on success it calls mlx4_en_moderation_update. At out it unlocks state_lock, frees the temporary structure, calls netdev_features_change(dev) only when no error occurred, and returns the error (0 on success).
note: Slice was the tail of mlx4_en_reset_config (name elided); fixed under the real name per rule 6 after reading the whole function (3513-3604). Old prose described the same tail but not the early returns.

name: mlx4_en_create_rx_ring
prose: Allocates one RX ring for an mlx4 Ethernet port (en_rx.c:237-320; slice cut the head). It allocates the ring structure on NUMA node 'node' (kzalloc_node; failure logs and returns -ENOMEM without touching *pring), fills size, mask, stride and buffer size, creates a page pool (an error is returned as that error), registers an xdp_rxq with xdp_rxq_info_reg (a negative result goes to err_pp and the function then returns -ENOMEM, the initial value of err, not the registration's own error), registers the page-pool memory model (its error is returned), allocates the rx_info array (-ENOMEM) and the hardware queue resources with mlx4_alloc_hwq_res on the requested node (its error is returned). On success it records the ring buffer and the RX timestamp filter, stores the ring in *pring and returns 0. On any failure after the ring was allocated it unwinds exactly what was set up (rx_info, xdp_rxq registration, page pool, the ring itself), sets *pring = NULL and returns the error.
note: Reviewer (omits xdp_rxq_info_reg failure path; code returns err without assigning it) is right: 275-276 jumps to err_pp with err still equal to its initial -ENOMEM (244). Slice cut the head; real function 237-320.

name: mlx4_do_bond
prose: Switches an mlx4 device into or out of bonded (HA) mode and restarts the affected auxiliary devices (intf.c:162-238; slice cut the head). It returns -EOPNOTSUPP if the device lacks MLX4_DEV_CAP_FLAG2_PORT_REMAP. It then calls mlx4_disable_rx_port_check(dev, enable) and returns its error if non-zero. When enable is true it sets MLX4_FLAG_BONDED in dev->flags; when false it resets the virtual-to-physical port map with mlx4_virt2phy_port_map(dev, 1, 2) and, if that fails, returns the error with dev->flags unchanged (the bonded flag is not cleared), otherwise clears MLX4_FLAG_BONDED. It takes intf_mutex and, for each registered auxiliary device that has a bound driver with MLX4_INTFF_BONDING set, skips it on SR-IOV (mfunc) devices (so those are neither removed nor re-added), and otherwise removes it and adds it again (del_adev / add_adev); a failed add logs a warning, sets that slot to NULL and continues. It unlocks and returns 0, so a failed add_adev is not reported to the caller.
note: Reviewers: original (returns 0 even when add_adev fails; mfunc devices are skipped, not re-added) right: 210-216, 222-228, 237; round-15 (when enable=false and the map reset fails, flags are left unchanged) right: 179-183. The claim 'BONDED not guaranteed still set' is odd: the flag simply keeps its previous value. 2 right. Slice cut the head; real function 162-238.

name: mapping_destroy
prose: Releases a reference on a shared mlx5 mapping context and frees it when it was the last one (mapping.c:248-263, 'void mapping_destroy(struct mapping_ctx *ctx)'; the slice shows only the tail after the refcount test). It decrements ctx->refcount and returns without doing anything else if the count did not reach zero. When it reaches zero it takes shared_ctx_lock, removes ctx from the shared list and unlocks, flushes the context's delayed work (mapping_flush_work), destroys the xarray and the mutex and frees ctx with kfree. It returns nothing; ctx must not be used afterwards.
note: Slice began mid-function; fixed under the real name mapping_destroy (read 248-263). The old prose omitted the refcount test.

name: mlx5e_port_set_priority2buffer
prose: Programs the PPTB register (priority to buffer mapping) for port 1 of an mlx5 device (mlx5/core/en/port.c, 'int mlx5e_port_set_priority2buffer(struct mlx5_core_dev *mdev, u8 *buffer)'; the packet item is the body of this function without its head). buffer must point to 8 bytes, one buffer index per priority. It allocates two zeroed register-sized buffers (-ENOMEM, after freeing whichever was allocated, if either fails), queries the PPTB register for local port 1 with mlx5_core_access_reg (a query error is returned), copies the response into the input, sets local_port 1 and pm = 0xFF, packs the 8 priorities into prio_x_buff as 4 bits each (buffer[prio] << (4 * prio)) and writes the register with mlx5_core_access_reg (write flag set). It frees both buffers on every path and returns the status of the last register access or the earlier error: 0 on success.
note: Slice began mid-function and the packet item name was elided; fixed under the real name mlx5e_port_set_priority2buffer (read the whole function from the file). Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: mlx5e_port_manual_buffer_config
prose: Applies a DCB port-buffer change on an mlx5 port (mlx5/core/en/port_buffer.c, 'int mlx5e_port_manual_buffer_config(...)' at about lines 484-592; the packet name mlx5e_dcbnl_setbuffer is not the real name and the slice starts inside the function). change is a bitmask of MLX5E_PORT_BUFFER_CABLE_LEN, _PFC, _PRIO2BUFFER and _SIZE. It queries the current port buffer configuration into a local structure and returns that error if the query fails. For each requested change it updates only that local copy: cable length recomputes the xoff thresholds; PFC queries the current priority-to-buffer map and recomputes which buffers are lossy for pfc->pfc_en; PRIO2BUFFER recomputes lossy buffers for the current PFC enable (from global pause or the PFC query) with the new map; SIZE rejects with -EINVAL a request where a lossless buffer has size 0 or where the total exceeds the headroom plus the spare buffer, otherwise stores the sizes and recomputes thresholds. Any helper error is returned immediately, so nothing is written to the device before the first error. If no buffer update was requested but the xoff value differs from priv->dcbx.xoff, it recomputes thresholds and marks the buffers for update. If a buffer update is pending it writes the port buffer with port_set_buffer (error returned), then stores xoff in priv->dcbx.xoff (even if the following step fails) and, if a prio-to-buffer update was requested, writes it with mlx5e_port_set_priority2buffer and returns that result; otherwise returns 0.
note: Packet name wrong and slice starts mid-function; real function mlx5e_port_manual_buffer_config (read from line 440 to the end, 592). Old reviewers mechanical only (right).

name: mlx5e_qos_bytes_rate_check
prose: Checks that a requested QoS rate is at least the minimum the mlx5 driver supports (qos.c:16-24). mdev is only used for logging. If nbytes (bytes per second) is below BYTES_IN_MBIT (125000, i.e. 1 Mbit/s) it emits a qos_warn message with the requested and minimum rates and returns -EINVAL; otherwise it returns 0. It has no other side effects.
note: Contract omitted: mdev is a pointer used in the logging call, so the function does not meet the integers-only rule (rule 4). BYTES_IN_MBIT = 125000 per qos.h:9. Slice cut the head; real function 16-24.

name: mlx5e_rep_netevent_event
prose: Netevent notifier of an mlx5 representor's neighbour-update table (rep/neigh.c:202-267; slice cut the head). It returns NOTIFY_DONE on every path, including the paths that did work; it never returns NOTIFY_OK. For NETEVENT_NEIGH_UPDATE with a neighbour of a table other than ARP (or ND, when IPv6 is enabled) it returns NOTIFY_DONE at once; otherwise it allocates an update work item (mlx5e_alloc_neigh_update_work; if that returns NULL it returns NOTIFY_DONE with nothing queued) and queues it on priv->wq. For NETEVENT_DELAY_PROBE_TIME_UPDATE with a parameter set that has no device or belongs to another table it returns NOTIFY_DONE; otherwise it searches the neigh_list under rcu_read_lock for an entry whose neigh_dev equals p->dev, returns NOTIFY_DONE if there is none, and if there is one lowers neigh_update->min_interval to the new DELAY_PROBE_TIME when that is smaller and calls mlx5_fc_update_sampling_interval with it. Other events fall through to NOTIFY_DONE. So the function does have side effects (queued work, updated interval and flow-counter sampling).
note: Reviewers: round-1 (omits the NOTIFY_DONE path when mlx5e_alloc_neigh_update_work fails) right: 226-228; round-2 (claims no side effects; kzalloc failure triggers WARN_ON and no-nhe path frees work) mostly right about side effects: 230, 259-263 (the WARN_ON/free are in the callee which I did not read); round-15 (claims NOTIFY_DONE on every path, but handled events return NOTIFY_OK) WRONG: every return in this function is NOTIFY_DONE (224, 228, 245, 257, 266). 2 right, 1 wrong. Slice cut the head.

name: mlx5_tc_ct_init
prose: Creates the TC connection-tracking private state for an mlx5 eswitch/NIC (tc_ct.c:2288-2398; slice cut the head). It returns a struct mlx5_tc_ct_priv pointer on success and NULL on every failure, never an error code (the err values are discarded). It first calls mlx5_tc_ct_init_check_support (failure returns NULL), then kzalloc's the private structure and creates the zone and labels mappings, the global CT and CT-NAT tables (with warnings on failure), adds the CT-NAT miss group and rule, initialises the control lock, three rhashtables (zone, tuples, NAT tuples), an ordered workqueue and the flow-steering ops (mlx5_tc_ct_fs_init), and registers debugfs entries. Failures unwind via labels in reverse (workqueue, rhashtables, the two global tables, the two mappings, kfree), then return NULL. The CT-NAT miss group and miss rule created by tc_ct_add_ct_table_miss_rule are not removed on any of the failure paths after they exist (the rhashtable, workqueue and fs-init failures do not destroy them).
note: Round-15 reviewer (miss rule/group also not removed on workqueue and fs-init failure paths, not only rhashtable paths) is right: no label destroys ct_nat_miss_rule/ct_nat_miss_group (2376-2395). Slice cut the head; real function 2288-2398.

name: mlx5e_encap_put
prose: Drops one reference on an mlx5e encap entry (tc_tun_encap.c:491-502; slice cut the head). The caller must not hold esw->offloads.encap_tbl_lock, because the function takes it itself: it calls refcount_dec_and_mutex_lock(&e->refcnt, &esw->offloads.encap_tbl_lock), which decrements the count and acquires the mutex only if the count reaches zero. If the count did not reach zero it returns without the lock held and without changing anything else. If it reached zero it removes e from its route list (list_del) and the encap hash (hash_del_rcu), releases the mutex and then calls mlx5e_encap_dealloc(priv, e) outside the lock. It returns nothing.
note: Round-15 reviewer (code asserts encap_tbl_lock is already held and never acquires/releases it) is WRONG: 495 acquires it via refcount_dec_and_mutex_lock when the count hits zero and 499 releases it. Slice cut the head; real function 491-502.

name: mlx5e_xsk_setup_pool
prose: Enables or disables an AF_XDP buffer pool on one mlx5e queue (xsk/pool.c:220-230; the shown function is only a dispatcher). It returns -EINVAL without side effects if qid >= params->num_channels. Otherwise it returns mlx5e_xsk_enable_pool(priv, pool, qid) when pool is non-NULL or mlx5e_xsk_disable_pool(priv, qid) when it is NULL; both take priv->state_lock for the duration and return the result of the locked helper (the lock is taken in those helpers, not in this function). Enabling returns -EBUSY if the queue already has a pool (the existing pool stays registered and mapped), -EINVAL if the pool is not usable or the parameters are not valid, an error from DMA-mapping or registering the pool, or the error of opening the XSK channel objects when the interface is open with an XDP program, undoing the pool registration and mapping on those later failures. Disabling returns -EINVAL if the queue has no pool and otherwise tears down the XSK objects (if open), removes and unmaps the pool and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original (omits enable/disable errors -EBUSY, -EINVAL, -ENOMEM besides qid range) right (errors come from the helpers, 79-148); round-15 (-EBUSY leaves the existing pool registered and DMA-mapped) right: pool.c:86-87 returns before any change. Old prose attributed state_lock to this function; the lock is taken in mlx5e_xsk_enable_pool/disable_pool (186-206). Slice cut the head; real function 220-230.
